_readme: The behind-the-desk shelf. Three tiers, one judgement per item, recorded once.
reference   -- present on EVERY host. Bounded by ceiling_bytes. If you cannot
work without it and it is small, it lives here.
circulating -- fetched where needed, not everywhere. Recorded so it is findable.
storage     -- one copy plus backup. NEVER synced. Recorded so nobody re-audits
82G to discover it was 82G of things they did not want.
The point of listing storage-tier items is that a catalogue covers what you do
NOT hold. On 2026-08-19 finding one 140K directory cost a survey of ~82G because
'reproducible' means it can be regenerated or re-downloaded from a stated source.
Reproducible items are never reference tier however useful, because the shelf is
for things that would otherwise be lost.
'bytes' is APPARENT size (sum of file sizes), matching what library-check.py measures. Storage-tier figures are du(1) disk usage and approximate -- they exist for magnitude only.

This file had to be force-added: futon0/.gitignore:3 is a blanket 'data/'. The catalogue of git-invisible material was itself made git-invisible, and the first commit silently dropped it -- git printed a hint, the commit succeeded on the other file, and the checker shipped to Zone with nothing to read. Same convention as data/git_sources.json and the other four force-added ledgers here: if you add an item to this shelf that lives under an ignored path, check `git ls-files` afterwards rather than trusting that `git commit` succeeded.
